item.title: 2nd Annual Holiday Sip + Shop
item.description: Tue Dec 1 2026, 6:00pm EST - Tue Dec 1 2026, 8:00pm EST
item.content:encoded:
Join us at Arts Collab Medford for our FREE  Holiday Sip + Shop, the ultimate neighborhood festive gathering. Browse a curated selection of handmade treasures, unique crafts, fine art, and one-of-a-kind gifts created by 30 talented artists who live and work right here in Medford.

What to Expect:

  • Shop Local Art: Discover everything from handcrafted jewelry, ceramics, and prints to cozy textiles and festive decor—perfect for everyone on your list (and maybe a little treat for yourself!).

  • Sip & Mingle: Enjoy seasonal drinks and light refreshments while you stroll through the shop and catch up with friends and neighbors.

  • Support Medford Creators: Every gift you purchase directly supports our local arts community and the creative neighbors who make Medford vibrant.

Grab your friends, raise a glass to the season, and cross off your holiday gift list in the heart of your community!

item.title: World Poetry Salon
item.description: Thu Dec 3 2026, 7:00pm EST - Thu Dec 3 2026, 8:30pm EST
item.content:encoded:
Free

Learn about modern poetry with short poems from some of the most celebrated writers of the twentieth century. We’ll listen to or read the poems, share initial impressions, and discuss whatever questions or themes emerge. The texts will be provided at the meeting—no homework required!

In December we’ll feature Primo Levi of Italy and Miroslav Holub of the Czech Republic.

This free salon-style series welcomes everyone—whether you’re well-versed in poetry or simply curious. Drop in for one session or all; each 90-minute meetup stands on its own. Prior experience with poetry will be helpful but isn’t required. An interest in innovative techniques, tolerance for ambiguity, and appreciation of different points of view will also be helpful.

Emphasis will be given to poets who bore witness to social upheaval and shaped modern literature with their responses to historical events. We will take a global perspective and include many writers in different languages who have been translated into English. Brief introductions to the poets will be offered, but no stuffy lectures; we’ll make connections and discoveries together through our sharing of questions and observations.

Hosted by Gary Roberts, a poet and co-founder of Arts Collaborative Medford, as part of our literary arts initiative. Bring your coffee, tea, or notebook and join us for a relaxed, open conversation about how poetry can reflect, resist, and reimagine the world around us.

item.title: Drawn Together: Art of Aging
item.description: Thu Dec 10 2026, 6:30pm EST - Thu Dec 10 2026, 8:00pm EST
item.content:encoded:
Free to the public

Join us for Drawn Together: The Art of Aging,  a facilitated discussion circle exploring our experiences of aging through art and shared reflection. Using works from The Art of Aging exhibition as a starting point, we’ll create space for an open, non-taboo conversation about the cultural narratives that shape how we experience aging, what we’re ready to let go of, and what we hope to welcome in. Together, we’ll imagine new ways of understanding aging and consider what it means to age creatively, on our own terms.

item.title: An Evening of Scottish Fiddle
item.content:encoded:
An Evening of Scottish Fiddle; featuring Isabel Oliart & Kyra Davies with Eamon Sefton on guitar

Tickets: $20 in advance, $25 at door, $15 for seniors

This concert is part of the Trad on the Mystic organized by Ellery Klein and hosted at Arts Collaborative Medford

 

Isabel Oliart is a Boston-based fiddler spanning the the worlds of Classical and Celtic fiddle music. She earned a BA from New England Conservatory in 2019, and an MA in Violin Performance from Boston University in 2024, where she also won the Bach Competition. 
She won the 2025 National Scottish Fiddle Championship, and has been a first-place winner of the New Hampshire Highland Games Fiddle Competition (2023), and the Scottish F.I.R.E. Composition Competition (2021). Isabel’s music has been featured on GBH’s A Celtic Sojourn and on NPR’s Says You. She has released two albums: ‘Late Evening’s Dram’ and ‘Tartan Rants and Rhapsodies’. She has performed at the Rockport Celtic Festival, Groton Hill Music Center, BCM fest, the Burren, Club Passim, the Loon Mountain Highland Games, and numerous other venues across New England. She was also part of the Boston Philharmonic Orchestra for many years and has subbed with the Albany Symphony and the New World Symphony Orchestra. 
 
Kyra Davies is a Boston-based violinist and fiddler whose multilayered performance career has taken her from San Diego, California to Siena, Italy. She can be found performing in arenas, concert halls, intimate house venues, or circus tents, with artists including The Who and the Eagles, symphony orchestras, chamber ensembles, and bands. Kyra specializes in contemporary music and has premiered dozens of pieces, both as a chamber musician and with the Boston Modern Orchestra Project.
In 2025, Kyra was crowned the New England Regional Open Scottish Fiddle Champion. With her duo project Mrs. Wilberforce and other groups, she has performed music from Scotland, Ireland, and other Celtic-influenced traditions at venues around New England. She regularly accompanies Scottish country dances and leads Scottish and Irish sessions.
 
Guitarist Eamon Sefton was born and raised on traditional music from Ireland, Scotland, and Cape Breton and has established himself as one of the top fretted instrument players in the American Celtic music scene. In addition to being a master of several acoustic instruments, Eamon is a heartfelt singer/songwriter. He has performed both locally and internationally with some of the top traditional musicians inside and out of the US, including Liz Carroll, Alasdair Fraser, John Doyle, Hanneke Cassel and many others. Eamon was the 2026 champion of the adult Accompaniment category at the all-Ireland traditional music CCE competitions held in Belfast.

item.title: The Jam Down By Riverside (potluck)
item.description: Sun Dec 13 2026, 1:00pm EST - Sun Dec 13 2026, 4:00pm EST
item.content:encoded:
The Jam Down By Riverside is a direct descendant of the now defunct Blues Jam at the Porch Southern Fare & Juke Joint, which was a descendant of the Johnny D’s blues jam. The jam is for building community and building skills. We welcome people of all ages, abilities, styles and instruments to join in the jamming. We do not have a strict Blues Only jam rule, but probably 85% of the repertoire is blues or blues-derived music. Please come to play or listen.

 The jams are on the Second Sundays of the month from 1-4pm.

We’re putting out a special call to teachers and their students to join us and we’re specifically trying to facilitate connections between people with more experience and folks with less experience.

What to expect:
The Jam is first come – first served, meaning you get into the pool to play when you arrive and sign up. There will be 3-4 different groups per hour depending on attendance. More people = shorter sets and more sets, so more people are able to play. The host will put different bands together based on the abilities and instrumentation available from the attendees. Each group will have a bandleader (often the lead vocalist) who will call songs, solos, starts, breaks and endings.

This is a potluck event, so bring food to share or bring you own eats. We will have beverages for sale for your convenience.

Please Do bring your own instrument, cable, sticks, microphone, and small harp amps.
Please Do not bring your own guitar amp and unless you have talked to the host in advance.

Volunteers will provide the following backline for players: drumkit, bass rig, 2 guitar amps, 2 direct boxes, microphones, monitors, PA system. We are taking donations of various equipment for backline. Please inquire about a donation. In particular we are looking for a small drumset and <15w guitar amps or modeling pedals.

We will ask for donations to offset the cost of the event and to show support for our organization.

item.title: Aging Together: Group Meeting and Presentation
item.content:encoded:
Free - Open to the public. 

This month, in conjuction with the Art of Aging exhibit, we are hosting a conversation of a local community group that gathers to support each other around aging in place. 

Aging Together offers monthly public gatherings for older people in the Medford area to hear speakers on topics related to aging, to learn about resources, and to get to know their neighbors.  The gatherings are held at the Medford Public Library and are organized by an all-volunteer planning group. Topics have ranged from those related to aging at home, such as shared living and services offered to seniors by local organizations, to how to be a Dementia Friend, to palliative care.
